question: The cause of being the refractive index(u) of transparent medium > 1, is:

options.text: Speed of light in vacuum < speed of light in transparent medium
Wavelength of light gets change as it moves from denser to rarer medium
Speed of light in vacuum > speed of light in transparent medium
Speed of light in vacuum = speed of light in transparent medium

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Speed of light in vacuum > speed of light in transparent medium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **refractive index** (denoted as **μ**) of a medium is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum (**c**) to the speed of light in that medium (**v**).
 
• The formula is: **μ = c/v**.
 
• Since the speed of light in a vacuum is always greater than its speed in any transparent medium, the refractive index is always **greater than 1**.
 
• The refractive index indicates how much the light bends when it enters a medium from another medium (such as air to glass).
 
• A higher refractive index implies that the medium is optically denser, causing light to slow down more significantly.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because light interacts with the particles in the medium, which affects its propagation speed.
 
• Examples of materials with a high refractive index include **diamond** (μ ≈ 2.42) and **glass** (μ ≈ 1.5).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Speed of light in vacuum = speed of light in transparent medium**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect as the speed of light in a vacuum is the universal constant (**c ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s**) and is always faster than its speed in any other medium.
 
• In any transparent medium like water, glass, or diamond, light slows down due to interactions with the medium's particles.

• **Wavelength of light gets change as it moves from denser to rarer medium**__
 
 
• While the wavelength of light does change when it moves between media of different refractive indices, this is not the direct cause of the refractive index being greater than 1.
 
• The change in wavelength is a result of the speed of light changing, which is explained by the refractive index.
